text:
emma_support: Heads up — AcmeHealth just flagged a big billing spike for streaming requests. They say lots of mid-stream disconnects are being counted as 5xx and billed. customer provided sample req id: req_0a1b2c3d
lina_eng: Ack. Can you paste the raw logs/headers they sent? This sounds similar to the chunked/EOF misclassification but let's confirm.
emma_support: Pasted from customer (redacted):
```
GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
User-Agent: acme-client/2.4
...

server log: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: api
```
mike_sre: That upstream message usually means the backend closed before we completed reading the response. Could be a client FIN racing with backend write. Do we have gateway traces for req_0a1b2c3d? 
opsgateway_bot: Trace found: trace_id=tr_6f9b2; route=/v1/generate; backend_status=200; gateway_label=STREAM_TRUNCATED; client_conn_closed=true
lina_eng: Interesting — backend returned 200 but gateway labeled as STREAM_TRUNCATED and then our billing pipeline treats STREAM_TRUNCATED as 5xx. That's likely the miscount.
raj_billing: Why are we mapping STREAM_TRUNCATED -> 5xx? That seems aggressive for client-initiated aborts.
mike_sre: Historically it was lumped into 5xx because we couldn't reliably tell if it was server crash vs client abort. But we now have client_conn_closed flag in traces.
chris_runtime: Quick repro I used locally to trigger the race (Linux):
```
# start a small server that streams indefinitely
python3 -c "import sys,time
print('HTTP/1.1 200 OK\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\n\n2\nok\n0\n');sys.stdout.flush();time.sleep(0.5); # then close"
# client: open connection and close mid-stream
```
curl --no-buffer http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -H "Accept: text/event-stream" & sleep 0.1; kill -9 $!

chris_runtime: Repro is flaky but consistent enough to validate the race.
emma_support: Customer wants credits; they reported ~18k requests labeled 5xx in the last 24h corresponding to streaming calls. Can we confirm they were client disconnects before issuing credits?
lina_eng: Actionable plan:
1) Short term: change billing classification to exclude traces where client_conn_closed=true AND backend_status in [200,206] from 5xx bucket. This will fix accounting for historical and near-term spikes. @raj_billing will that pass audit? 
2) Medium: patch gateway to emit a clearer event STREAM_CLIENT_ABORT vs STREAM_SERVER_ABORT and update metrics.
3) Long: adjust EOF heuristic to prefer backend_status/headers when available so we don't default to 5xx on truncated stream.

raj_billing: (1) sounds reasonable but need a log sampling to verify we aren't hiding real server failures. If we can show backend_status=200 for the sampled events, we can issue credits.
mike_sre: I'll run a quick query to sample 1000 events for the customer and count backend_status distribution. Give me ~30m.
emma_support: FYI customer already escalated to their finance team. They're expecting a resolution timeline.
chris_runtime: Also note: some clients (mobile SDKs) do a hard TCP FIN after receiving enough tokens; in edge cases the kernel will send FIN before we record final chunk. We should be careful with heuristics that assume any truncated stream = upstream 5xx.
lina_eng: Could we do a non-invasive patch tonight: change classification only for the hosted API (not Dedicated) and only for routes with chunked encoding? That reduces blast radius.
mike_sre: Agree. I'll prepare a canary: billing classification tweak + updated alerting. Canary in us-east-1 10% traffic for 1h.
raj_billing: After we run the sampling and confirm 95% of those spikes have backend_status 200/206 + client_conn_closed=true, we'll process credits for the window customer asked about. Please log the sampling query id.
emma_support: Customer reply: "Thanks — we'll wait for your sample and proposed credits. Please keep us updated; this is material to our month-end." :worried: 
lina_eng: Assigned: @mike_sre run sampling + canary; @chris_runtime open a runtime PR to split STREAM_TRUNCATED into CLIENT_ABORT/SERVER_ABORT (link later); @raj_billing prepare credit procedure. I'll draft a short KB note for support.
mike_sre: I kicked off the sampling job: sample_job_id=samp_20240318_001. Early peek: ~92% of flagged events have backend_status in {200,206} and client_conn_closed=true. I'll post final numbers in 25m after full run.
emma_support: Perfect, thx. I'll tell AcmeHealth we have a canary and sampling in progress and we'll follow up with concrete credits once you confirm numbers.
lina_eng: Small follow-up: add a metric for "stream.client_abort_vs_server_abort" so billing can consume it directly. That will avoid heuristic gaps.
chris_runtime: I'll include a minimal reproducer in the PR and add e2e for the gateway's classification path.
opsgateway_bot: Deploy scheduled: canary-billing-fix -> us-east-1 @ 2024-03-18T23:30Z (10% traffic). Rollback window 30m.
emma_support: Thanks team. I'll update the customer after the canary. Closing thread for now but will reopen if anything surprising shows up.
